subject: Core priorities outlook + escalation requests
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Core priorities outlook + escalation requests

Team — quick weeknote with wins, near-term risks, and asks for the leadership distro. Keeping concise so we can surface decisions in tomorrow’s ops sync.

WINS
- Redwood Dedicated benchmarking: 3% lower p95 on standard inference loads after kernel tuning (SRE + Runtime). This preserves predicted unit economics for our Q4 commit.
- Acme POC: initial throughput tests passed (attached summary), queued for pilot next week.

RISKS
- Capacity tightness for the next two weeks in us-west: two hosts with degraded NVLink performance; we’re running degraded autoscale thresholds. Risk to p95 for high-concurrency routes.
- Potential quality regressions for a Canary quantized variant — early evals show ~1.5% ROUGE drop on a targeted prompt set.

ASKS (decision lanes)
1) SLA exception for two-week capacity shortfall (need approval to route burst to reserved pods in us-east while NVLink issue is diagnosed). I’ve attached the draft exemption form.
2) Approve 1.0 FTE temporary SRE support (contractor) to run the NVLink remediation and on-call for the pilot.
3) Greenlight limited rollout of quantized variant to 5% traffic with rollback guardrails; if we see >2% quality delta, auto-fallback to baseline.

Attachments: q4_okr_readout_v2.pdf (summary + metrics), detailed NVLink incident notes are in the shared Drive link below.

Next steps I propose: if we get approval on (1) and (2) by EOD today we can implement the routing change and schedule contractor onboarding for tomorrow.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Core priorities outlook + escalation requests

Thanks Diego — good summary. A couple quick clarifications before I escalate: 

- For the SLA exception, what is the expected additional cost to routing to reserved pods in us-east for the 2-week window? Ballpark monthly pro-rated figure is fine.
- For the contractor SRE request, can you confirm whether this is a Redwood headcount ask (temp convert) or a third-party contractor and the budget code?
- On the quantized variant: can you add the targeted prompt set for the eval and the mitigation checklist we’ll use if quality drops post-rollout?

If you can reply with those numbers I’ll route to Finance + Legal for a fast approval path.

On scope: please keep the Acme pilot communications minimal until we confirm the routing change — procurement is looped on their side.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Core priorities outlook + escalation requests

Laura — answers inline and added the exemption form.

- Cost: routing to reserved us-east capacity adds an estimated $16k pro-rated over two weeks (usage + data transfer estimates); Finance flagged ~5% variance but ok under the emergency cap.
- SRE support: third-party contractor (vendor: AltusOps) for two weeks; budget code OP-PLAT-2026-Q4. We have a contractor quote attached (I’ve added SLA exemption form: sla_exemption_form.docx).
- Quantized variant mitigations: target prompt set is the Q4-evals-v2 (Drive link). Rollback checklist included in attachment — auto-fallback + canary health monitor.

I’m attaching the filled exemption form and a 1-page cost note. If Legal/Finance bless, we’ll schedule the routing change tonight and start contractor onboarding tomorrow morning.

Forwarded attachment stubs: sla_exemption_form.docx (filled)
Related link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Q4_OKR_READOUT

Diego
